:::{#exm-fitting-procedure}
#### Inputs of two fitting procedures

Least-squares polynomial fitting of degree $\polydeg$ has these inputs:

- [data set](#def-data-set) $\dataset$: the observations the polynomial is fitted to;
- [model family](#def-model-family) $\modelfam$: the polynomials of degree at most $\polydeg$;
- [objective function](#def-objective-function) $\objfn$: the [residual sum of squares](correlation-regression.qmd#def-rss);
- [optimization algorithm](#def-optimization-algorithm) $\optalg$: solving the [normal equations](correlation-regression.qmd#def-normal-equations), which finds the unique minimizer exactly;
- [random seed](#def-random-seed) $\seed$: none, since nothing is random;
- [tuning parameter](#def-tuning-parameter) $\tuning$: the degree $\polydeg$;
- [preprocessing](#def-preprocessing) $\featmap$: none.

Because the minimizer is unique and exact, the family, the data and the objective already determine the fitted rule.

The [cross-validation choice procedure](#def-cv-choice) over polynomials of several degrees is different:

- data set $\dataset$: the observations the candidates are fitted and scored on;
- model family $\modelfam$: the polynomials of every candidate degree;
- objective function $\objfn$: the residual sum of squares within each candidate, and the [cross-validation estimate](#def-cv-estimate-indexed) between candidates;
- optimization algorithm $\optalg$: the normal equations for each candidate, then keeping the candidate with the smallest estimate;
- random seed $\seed$: fixes the random [fold assignment](#def-fold-assignment);
- tuning parameter $\tuning$: none, since cross-validation chooses the degree;
- preprocessing $\featmap$: none.

Here two seeds give two fold assignments, which can choose different degrees and so give different fitted rules from the same data.

:::
